response.markdown_report:
The recommended first experiment remains **attribute-preserving text fusion within HSTU**, targeting overly broad matches and compatibility mismatches while testing Electronics separation. “Preserving” means retaining informative tokens; it does not establish attribute understanding or compatibility.

### Insights and framework

Three starting-point insights guide selection. First, useful recommendations extend a specific recent purpose; broad historical similarity is insufficient. Second, titles/descriptions may expose connectors, dimensions and formats, but missing specifications remain unknown. Third, Electronics has a 10.71% sampled wrong-rank rate and −0.0749 tenth-percentile margin. Embedding scores near 0.5 do not support collapse regularization; large margins elsewhere do not establish held-out accuracy.

Three literature insights refine implementation. HSTU supplies the retained sequential backbone [1]. HSTU-BLaIR motivates text fusion, but its pretrained encoder provides no scratch-training guarantee [2]. MARS motivates attribute distinctions [3]; ConvMF and Ask the GRU support investigating ordered text encoders in different tasks [6–7]. Mean pooling loses order, number–unit associations and negation scope; TedRec motivates testing fusion rather than assuming addition helps [8].

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Gap and proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal intent | HSTU; TLSRec [4] | Recent-purpose gating; fulfilled needs remain unobserved |
| Item specificity | HSTU-BLaIR; MARS | Scratch-trained text fusion; compare pooling with local CNN phrases |
| Ranking supervision | Sampled-softmax analysis [5] | Moderate hard negatives; monitor false negatives and saturation |

### Candidate assessment

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each pair gives a strength and limitation.

- **Mean-text fusion: 4/7/8/7/6.** Originality: constrained adaptation, established mechanism. Potential: reusable specificity, weak rare-token supervision. User: targets broad matches/compatibility, loses attribute relations. Model: may separate Electronics items, indirect evidence. Difficulty: small encoder, substantial serialization/diagnostic care.
- **Recent-history gate: 4/7/7/5/4.** Originality: focused adaptation, familiar gating. Potential: transferable intent, sparse histories. User: addresses stale associations/redundancy, completed needs unlabeled. Model: contextual discrimination, indirect evidence. Difficulty: compact module, causal alignment matters.
- **Moderate hard negatives: 3/7/5/9/3.** Originality: focused objective, established approach. Potential: efficient discrimination, false negatives. User: distinguishes alternatives, adds no compatibility evidence. Model: targets weak margins, training gains may mislead. Difficulty: modest sampler, mining cost.
- **CNN-text fusion: 4/7/8/7/7.** Originality: ordered phrases, established encoder. Potential: local attribute associations, sparse supervision. User: specificity/compatibility, no guaranteed understanding. Model: confusing-item separation, unverified here. Difficulty: compact convolution, extra tuning/runtime.

### Selected experiment

At 0% progress, retain mean-text fusion as the simplest primary contrast against corrected HSTU. CNN fusion is a subsequent experiment if budget permits. Both target broad thematic substitution and compatibility mismatches; Electronics separation is the model-facing hypothesis. Neither labels fulfilled needs.

```text
text(i) = project(masked_mean(trainable_tokens(title_description(i))))
item(i) = ID(i) + sigmoid(gate) * normalize(text(i))
features = unchanged_HSTU(item(left_padded_history))
score(i) = dot(features[final_nonpadding_position], item(i))
```

Keep baseline loss/sampling and scoring normalization. Prespecify tokenization, vocabulary, missingness, checkpoint opportunities and selection rules. Preserve one checkpoint/category, routing, seeds, limits, predictor parity and diagnostic interfaces. Track branch norms/gate saturation and paired validation hits. Training-only shuffled-text and capacity controls can investigate shortcuts if budget permits; treat validation gains as exploratory because repeated selection creates optimism [9]. Sampled HR@10 and twenty training-user recommendations answer different questions [10]. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Train one HSTU per category with a small, jointly learned title/description encoder fused into item-ID representations. Use the identical fused representation for historical items and candidate scoring. Make mean pooling the primary experiment; reserve an order-sensitive CNN for a separately trained follow-up if the compute budget permits.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad thematic substitution and practical compatibility mismatches. Electronics has the weakest measured sampled separation: a 10.71% wrong-rank rate, −0.0749 tenth-percentile margin and 16.36% small-margin rate. Available text could expose distinctions absent from item IDs, but retaining tokens does not establish compatibility understanding. Mean pooling cannot preserve token order, number–unit binding or negation scope. Values near 0.5 for the mapped embedding similarity statistic provide little evidence of directional collapse. Strong training margins in other categories do not establish held-out HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected HSTU backbone, causal masks, baseline loss, sampler, optimizer and existing score normalization for the primary contrast. Do not replace HSTU with another backbone. Train exactly one independent model per category; internal text and ID branches are jointly optimized parts of that network. Never combine checkpoints, separately fitted scores or independent predictors.

Use only supplied titles/descriptions and public training histories; ignore the generic input examples offering ratings, reviews, categories, prices or stores because those fields are unavailable in this task. No pretrained encoder or external dataset is permitted. Build each category vocabulary from metadata for items appearing in its training histories. Apply Unicode NFKC normalization and lowercase; tokenize with the Python regex pattern [^\W_]+(?:[./+−-][^\W_]+)*|[^\s\w], preserving digits, punctuation-bearing identifiers and unit tokens where possible. Reserve PAD=0 and UNK=1, retain tokens with frequency at least two, cap the vocabulary at 50,000 including reserved tokens, and order by descending frequency then lexical order. Cache at most the first 32 title tokens and first 96 description tokens; store field boundaries and preprocessing version. Frequency filtering and truncation can still erase rare compatibility details, which must be reported as limitations. Do not access held-out interaction files to build this vocabulary. Map vocabulary-OOV tokens to UNK and absent text to an empty mask.

Use 64-dimensional randomly initialized token embeddings with padding_idx=0. Compute a masked mean across the retained tokens and a bias-free projection to the existing HSTU item dimension. Define t as the projected text vector normalized with an epsilon-stabilized L2 norm. Fuse as e_ID + sigmoid(a) * t, initializing a=-2, without changing the baseline's subsequent item/scoring normalization. This bounded scalar gate is a proposed experimental setting, not a published HSTU optimum. Missing-text items receive exactly zero text contribution; padding IDs receive exactly zero fused representation. Cache token IDs rather than detached text representations so encoder gradients remain live. Log ID/text branch norms and the gate to detect branch domination or an unused text encoder. Mean pooling is deliberately limited to token presence; it does not claim relational attribute modeling.

Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items), including their existing dimensional and broadcasting conventions. item_emb remains the raw trainable ID embedding; candidate scoring must use the effective fused representation. Any probe that measures item_emb alone must explicitly label its statistic as raw-ID geometry. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), with measured metrics and their definitions. view.model must remain the actual trained nn.Module. Handle train_loader tuples (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L; evaluate valid positive positions through predict_score. Keep the family-specific sample_batch and host ModelView contracts. Do not fabricate metadata category breakdowns; mark unavailable attribution as unavailable. Compute sequential readout using the greatest index where sequence is nonzero, never count minus one. Handle empty histories explicitly using the baseline's deterministic fallback. During next-item training retain all valid position-aligned targets rather than replacing them with a single readout.

Serialize token vocabulary, per-item token IDs/masks, preprocessing version, gate, dimensions, architecture configuration and all weights with each category checkpoint. Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical encoder, normalization, missing-text handling, readout and category routing. Verify score agreement between the in-memory model and reloaded predictor on a fixed permitted training-prefix batch. Each category must load exactly one checkpoint. Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Preserve the fixed splits and pinned evaluator with 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42.

Prespecify the primary contrast as corrected ID-only HSTU versus gated mean-text HSTU. Use identical validation opportunities at epochs 50, 100, 150 and 200; select one checkpoint per category by its validation HR@10, breaking ties toward the earlier epoch, and compare the resulting equally weighted four-category macro HR@10. Declare a 0.005 absolute macro improvement as the minimum worthwhile exploratory gain before inspecting results. Log every validation look and all failed runs. If the host exposes paired per-user hit indicators without modifying its evaluator, retain identical-user/candidate pairs, report category changes and discordant counts, and use 10,000 paired bootstrap replicates with analysis seed 42 for a conditional 95% macro-difference interval. Resample within category, or by shared user identity if identities overlap categories. Exact McNemar tests are optional secondary analyses. These analyses exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty and do not correct adaptive checkpoint/architecture selection. If paired outputs are unavailable, do not reconstruct or invent them.

Profile throughput before committing to additional contrasts; charge training, diagnostics, debugging and failures against the aggregate 43,200 GPU-second allowance. Four concurrent slots reduce elapsed time without expanding that budget. Record validation score versus cumulative GPU-seconds. Follow-ups, only if affordable, are: the same fusion with a small width-2/3 CNN; parameter-matched ID-only HSTU with an active residual MLP; and retraining the same text architecture after deterministic complete-text permutation among nonmissing items within category. Refine the permutation by training-popularity and text-length bins if feasible, preserving missingness. An identifier-stripping aligned-versus-shuffled comparison can investigate memorization. These are separate experiments, each retaining one checkpoint/category, never fused predictions. Match tokenization, scoring and training opportunities; also report actual compute because architecture throughput differs. Such controls investigate text alignment and capacity, but do not prove semantic transfer. Optional attribute-sensitive examples must come from permitted training metadata, be labeled qualitative, and never substitute for validation HR@10. The twenty real training-user full-catalog recommendations remain qualitative diagnostics, not independent accuracy evidence. No test data or other-trial checkpoints may be read.
idea.pseudocode:
Prespecify the primary baseline-versus-text contrast and validation schedule.
For each of Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl:
  Retain the supplied split and preprocessing seed 0.
  Build deterministic title/description vocabulary from training-item metadata.
  Cache bounded token IDs and masks; reserve PAD and UNK.
  Initialize corrected HSTU and text parameters with training seed 42.
  Define item_repr(ids):
    pooled = masked_mean(token_embedding(tokens[ids]), token_mask[ids])
    text = L2_normalize(bias_free_projection(pooled), eps=1e-8)
    text = text * has_text[ids]
    fused = item_emb(ids) + sigmoid(gate) * text
    return baseline_item_normalization(fused) * (ids != 0)
  Define log2feats(sequence):
    return existing_HSTU_backbone(item_repr(sequence), existing_causal_masks)
  Define predict_score(features, items):
    return existing_score_rule(features, item_repr(items))
  Train position-aligned targets with baseline loss/sampling:
    use 200 batches/epoch, at most 200 epochs, one GPU
    preserve existing regularization and optimizer
  At epochs 50, 100, 150, 200:
    gather greatest nonpadding index for sequence prediction
    evaluate using the unchanged pinned validation evaluator
    log HR@10, cumulative GPU-seconds, branch norms and gate
  Retain one checkpoint by category validation HR@10; ties choose earlier epoch.
  Serialize model, vocabulary, token tables, masks and configuration.
  Write the identical architecture into the predictor writer.
  Verify in-memory versus reloaded scores on a training-prefix batch.
  Run family-compatible diagnostics with measured metric definitions.
Compare the equally weighted four-category validation HR@10 against baseline.
If host outputs permit, analyze paired user hits without changing evaluation.
Report gains as exploratory; reserve confirmation for the host's held-out evaluation.
Run separately trained controls or CNN follow-up only within remaining budget.

originality.positive: Provides a focused, constraint-compatible adaptation of text fusion to scratch-trained HSTU with explicit metadata, diagnostic and inference controls.
originality.negative: ID-plus-text fusion, masked pooling and scalar gating are established mechanisms; no new attribute-binding method is introduced.

future_potential.positive: Creates a controlled foundation for studying whether permitted text improves item specificity and whether ordered phrase encoders add useful distinctions.
future_potential.negative: Sparse token supervision, missing specifications and context-free pooling may limit gains; the approach does not identify fulfilled needs or guarantee compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary encoder is small and preserves the HSTU backbone, baseline objective and sampler.
code_difficulty.negative: Deterministic metadata alignment, effective-score diagnostics, bounded compute, checkpoint serialization and embedded predictor parity require substantial care.

related_work.title: [1] Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with pointwise attention, relative biases and multiplicative gating.
Provides the backbone retained throughout the proposed experiment.
limitations: Does not establish explicit detection of fulfilled needs or practical compatibility.
Does not establish gains for the supplied pinned Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: [2] HSTU-BLaIR
contributions: Adds projected text embeddings to trainable item-ID embeddings before HSTU.
Provides the closest architectural motivation for the selected fusion experiment.
Uses separately projected and normalized candidate representations.
limitations: Uses a frozen pretrained BLaIR encoder, unavailable under this task's constraints.
Does not establish effectiveness for randomly initialized token encoders or the proposed shared input/candidate representation.
Does not establish the proposed gate initialization, vocabulary, truncation or missing-text settings.

related_work.title: [3] MARS
contributions: Uses attribute-aware text representations and attribute-wise user–item matching.
Motivates retaining fine item distinctions that broad pooled similarity can obscure.
limitations: Relies on pretrained language modeling.
Does not demonstrate compatibility inference or gains for this constrained scratch-trained HSTU experiment.

related_work.title: [4] TLSRec
contributions: Models local and global preferences with a dimension-wise gate conditioned on elapsed time.
limitations: Temporal gating does not supply labels for fulfilled needs.
Reported findings do not establish improvements under the pinned evaluation.
Any temporal adaptation must use only timestamps available in the observed prefix.

related_work.title: [5] Sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: Analyzes how sampled-softmax training emphasizes informative negatives and how temperature affects gradient concentration.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal negative sampler or temperature for these categories.
Strong sampled training margins do not guarantee held-out HR@10.
Sampling corrections do not resolve unknown false-negative preferences.

related_work.title: [6] Convolutional Matrix Factorization for Document Context-Aware Recommendation
contributions: Provides indirect evidence that jointly learned CNN document features can help recommendation.
Motivates a small order-sensitive text encoder as a follow-up to mean pooling.
limitations: Studies rating prediction rather than the specified sequential HR@10 task.
Reported results are not a direct mean-pooling ablation or a test of model-number, unit and negation understanding.

related_work.title: [7] Ask the GRU: Multi-task Learning for Deep Text Recommendations
contributions: Compares an order-sensitive text encoder with averaged embeddings.
Reports improved cold-start recall in a scientific-paper recommendation setting.
limitations: Does not establish product-attribute preservation or practical compatibility.
Its task and evaluation differ from the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: [8] TedRec
contributions: Provides ablation evidence that text/ID fusion choices affect sequential recommendation.
Motivates testing adaptive fusion rather than assuming unscaled addition is sufficient.
limitations: Uses pretrained text representations.
Its random-text-vector variant is not a jointly trained randomly initialized token encoder.
Does not establish the proposed scalar gate as optimal.

related_work.title: [9] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit a finite validation criterion.
Supports prespecified comparisons, logged validation opportunities and exploratory interpretation of selected gains.
limitations: Does not provide a task-specific correction for this adaptive search.
Ordinary bootstrap intervals around the selected winner do not remove selection optimism.

related_work.title: [10] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled-candidate metrics can differ from full-catalog ranking comparisons.
Supports interpreting pinned HR@10 within its specified candidate protocol.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host evaluator.
Does not establish that full-catalog qualitative recommendations provide independent accuracy evidence.

related_work.title: Approximate Statistical Tests for Comparing Supervised Classification Learning Algorithms
contributions: Discusses paired statistical comparisons, including McNemar testing.
Supports examining discordant binary hit outcomes on identical users and candidate sets.
limitations: Conditional paired tests exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability.
Tests on adaptively selected models do not remove validation selection bias.

related_work.title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results
contributions: Motivates reporting performance alongside computational search effort.
Supports logging cumulative compute, failed trials and validation opportunities.
limitations: Does not prescribe an optimal allocation of the supplied GPU-second budget.
Equal epoch counts do not ensure equal compute across architectures.
